minutes.headline: Select Board approved the town manager's evaluation with a source-citing note after a long dispute; chair's last meeting.
minutes.summary: The meeting honored the departing chair, then approved an arts festival entertainment license and heard a quarterly revenue update. Most of the night was a heated debate over whether the town manager's self-evaluation text could stay in the board's composite review. The board marked up the document to identify those parts and endorsed it, announced a new salary for the town manager, and authorized a Green Communities grant MOU.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the chair, praised the Lane collection presentation at the library, and urged people to vote Saturday.
Rocks washing into the road at Pleasant Street and Mass Ave from a private property, a danger to cyclists and motorcycles; DPW cleans up at taxpayer expense.
Thanked the chair for his service and Memorial Day work.

what_happened.line: The Select Board endorsed a marked-up town manager performance evaluation, after a long dispute over including the manager's self-evaluation text.
The board agreed to add a note and italicize the parts of the review that came from a document the town manager prepared.
A vote to keep the self-evaluation in the document failed or was unclear, and the chair's ruling on it was disputed.
The chair announced a new salary for the town manager after the review; the amount is not given in the minutes.
The board approved the Arts Festival entertainment license with the fee waived, and endorsed a Green Communities planning grant MOU with MRPC.

why_it_matters: The town manager's pay and review are set here, and the pay comes from the town budget, mostly taxes, so the outcome affects what residents fund.
Several votes on the review were not audible in the captions, so the record of who voted how on the evaluation is incomplete.
watch_next: The signing of the final marked-up evaluation, which the board discussed doing at a posted meeting or on May 21.
The town manager's follow-up on the Pleasant Street runoff and on green arrows at the Walmart intersection.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the figures, the warrants, the Arts Festival license and the MRPC MOU. They differ on the self-evaluation and rating motions, where ours records no outcomes. The main thing to know is that the official minutes record a failed 2-2 vote to sign and submit the composite, and ours has that vote as "not audible", so check the recording.
